summaryEn: Hoya reads about eongan, the Hangul letters of Joseon: the oldest one found so far, from an officer far away to his wife, and the letters King Jeongjo wrote to his aunt from boyhood on.
hoyaIntroEn: Let's read letters that families in Joseon wrote in Hangul!
hoyaOutroEn: Now you know how Joseon families shared warm feelings in Hangul letters!
learningGoalsEn: Know that eongan is an old word for a letter written in Hangul in Joseon times.
Know that the Na Singeol Hangul Letter, from an officer to his wife, is the oldest Hangul letter found so far, and that it shows men and people far from the capital wrote Hangul too.
Know that King Jeongjo wrote Hangul letters to his aunt from boyhood on, and that the album is a Treasure at the National Hangeul Museum.
Read and recognize 편지 (pyeonji), 군관 (gungwan), 가족 (gajok), 외숙모 (oesungmo), 안부 (anbu) and 썼어요 (sseosseoyo).

scenes.narrationEn: King Jeongjo also wrote Hangul letters to his aunt, Lady Yeoheung Min. He began when he was a small boy and kept writing after he became king.

facts.claimEn: Eongan is an old word for a letter written in Hangul. It meant 'a letter in eonmun' and was used in a way that looked down on such letters.
facts.claimKo: 언간은 예전에 언문 편지라는 뜻으로, 한글로 쓴 편지를 낮잡아 이르던 말이다.

sources.title: 언간 — 표준국어대사전
sources.publisher: 국립국어원 (National Institute of Korean Language) — 표준국어대사전
sources.quoteOrLocator: "예전에, 언문 편지라는 뜻으로, 한글로 쓴 편지를 낮잡는 뜻으로 이르던 말."

facts.claimEn: The Na Singeol Hangul Letter is two sheets that Na Singeol, a junior military officer of early Joseon, wrote in Hangul to his wife, a woman of the Sinchang Maeng clan. When he wrote it, he seems to have been serving as a junior officer in Hamgyeong Province in the far north. The letter was found folded many times in her tomb.
facts.claimKo: 나신걸 한글편지는 조선 초기 군관 나신걸이 아내 신창맹씨에게 한글로 써서 보낸 편지 2장이다. 편지를 쓸 때 그는 함경도에서 하급 군관으로 근무한 것으로 보이며, 편지는 신창맹씨 묘에서 여러 번 접힌 상태로 발견되었다.

sources.title: 나신걸 한글편지 — 국가유산포털
sources.quoteOrLocator: "조선 초기 군관(軍官) 나신걸(羅臣傑, 1461∼1524)이 아내 신창맹씨(新昌孟氏)에게 한글로 써서 보낸 편지 2장"; "편지를 썼을 당시 그는 함경도에서 하급 군관으로 근무하고 있었던 것으로 보인다"; "피장자의 머리맡에서 여러 번 접힌 상태로 발견되었다"

facts.claimEn: The Na Singeol Hangul Letter is the oldest Hangul letter found so far, and it is designated a Treasure.
facts.claimKo: 나신걸 한글편지는 지금까지 발견된 한글 편지 가운데 가장 오래된 자료이며, 보물로 지정되어 있다.

sources.title: 나신걸 한글편지 — 국가유산포털
sources.quoteOrLocator: "‘나신걸 한글편지’는 현재까지 발견된 한글편지 가운데 가장 오래된 자료"; designation shown on the page: 보물

facts.claimEn: In the letter, Na Singeol mostly writes that he misses his mother and their children, asks his wife to send clothes he needs, such as a cheollik, and asks her to look after the farm work and small household matters.
facts.claimKo: 편지는 어머니와 자녀들에 대한 그리움, 철릭 등 필요한 옷을 보내 달라는 부탁, 농사일과 소소한 집안일을 살펴 달라는 당부가 주를 이룬다.

sources.title: 나신걸 한글편지 — 국가유산포털
sources.quoteOrLocator: "내용은 모친과 자녀들에 대한 그리움, 철릭(天翼, 조선시대 무관이 입던 공복公服) 등 필요한 의복을 보내주고, 농사일을 잘 챙기며 소소한 가정사를 살펴봐 달라는 당부가 주를 이룬다."

facts.claimEn: The letter shows that Hangul had spread to the faraway border regions and to junior officials, and that men, too, used Hangul with ease, although Hangul in Joseon has often been thought of as mainly a script of women.
facts.claimKo: 이 편지는 한글이 먼 변방 지역과 하급 관리에게까지 널리 퍼졌음을 보여 주며, 한글이 여성 중심의 글로 여겨진 것과 달리 남성들도 한글을 익숙하게 썼음을 보여 준다.

sources.title: 나신걸 한글편지 — 국가유산포털
sources.quoteOrLocator: "한양에서 멀리 떨어진 변방지역과 하급관리에게까지 한글이 널리 보급되었음을 말해 준다"; "조선 시대 한글이 여성 중심의 글이었다고 인식된 것과 달리 ... 남성들 역시 한글을 익숙하게 사용했음을 보여 준다"

facts.claimEn: King Jeongjo wrote letters in Hangul to Lady Yeoheung Min, his aunt (the wife of his mother's eldest brother), from when he was a small boy, through his years as the royal heir, to his years as king. They are collected in one album.
facts.claimKo: 정조는 원손 시절부터 세손 시절, 왕위에 있던 시절까지 큰외숙모 여흥 민씨에게 한글로 편지를 썼고, 이 편지들은 한 첩으로 모여 있다.

authorNotes: Names follow F-CNT-002 (no hyphens): Na Singeol (나신걸), Jeongjo, Lady Yeoheung Min (여흥 민씨). Left out on purpose: the dates and ages (1461-1524, the 1490s dating, 2011 find, Jeongjo 1752-1800), so no fact needs a second numeric source; the tomb is named only in f2 (reference zone) and the narration says the letter was found long afterwards, folded many times, so no scene names a burial. The heritage portal names the album 정조 한글어찰첩 and the museum names it 정조어필한글편지첩; the story says only "an album". The MCST press release says Jeongjo's Hangul letters survive in the original only in this album; that claim is left out because it is about surviving originals among his letters and is easy to misread. 큰외숙모 is the wife of the mother's eldest brother (Hyegyeonggung Hong's eldest brother); the story says "his aunt". The 2025 exhibition page (hangeul.go.kr/exhibition/643) is a touring show held at the Chungcheongnam-do History Museum; it is cited only for its statement about families sharing feelings in Hangul.
